payload.scenario: A jar of muddy pond water needs to be cleaned up in stages. Match each stage to what it does.

slots.label: Letting the jar sit untouched for an hour
Pouring the clearer water through a cloth
Heating the filtered water until it boils away

components.label: Evaporation — removes the water, leaving dissolved salts behind
Filtration — traps remaining fine particles
Sedimentation — heavier mud settles to the bottom

payload.hint: The order matters: settle the heavy stuff first, then filter what's left, then deal with what's actually dissolved.

payload.scenario: Match each continent to the fact that actually describes it.

components.label: A continent located entirely underwater beneath the Pacific Ocean
The coldest continent, almost entirely covered by a thick sheet of ice, with no permanent population
The continent crossed by the equator, home to the Sahara, the world's largest hot desert
The largest continent by both area and population, home to Mount Everest

payload.hint: One continent is the largest and most populated, one has the world's biggest hot desert, and one is permanently frozen.

payload.scenario: Match each geographic connection to what it actually means for travel or trade.

slots.label: The Indian Ocean lies between Africa, Asia and Australia
The Isthmus of Panama connects North and South America
The Suez Canal connects the Mediterranean Sea to the Red Sea

components.label: Means all three oceans are actually the exact same body of water
Lets ships travel between Europe and Asia without going all the way around Africa
Is a narrow strip of land that ships must sail around unless a canal is built through it
Makes it a major route for trade ships travelling between these three continents

payload.hint: Each geographic connection either enables trade routes or creates a barrier that a canal can solve.

payload.scenario: Match each ocean to the fact that actually describes it.

components.label: An ocean located entirely within the continent of Australia
The smallest and shallowest ocean, mostly covered in ice near the North Pole
The second-largest ocean, separating the Americas from Europe and Africa
The largest and deepest ocean on Earth, bordering Asia and the Americas

payload.hint: Think about size and location — one is the biggest by far, one connects the Americas to Europe/Africa, and one is small and icy.

title: Decline of the Harappan Civilisation → Effect

payload.scenario: Match each likely cause of Harappan decline to the effect it had on the civilisation.

slots.label: The course of a major river (like the Ghaggar-Hakra) dried up or shifted over time
Monsoon rainfall patterns weakened in the region
Trade routes with Mesopotamia gradually declined

components.label: The population of Harappan cities suddenly tripled in a few years
Harappan cities lost an important source of wealth and foreign goods
Agriculture that depended on regular rains became harder to sustain
Farming communities along the river had to abandon their settlements

payload.hint: Most theories about the decline point to environmental changes making the old way of life harder to sustain — not a sudden disaster.

payload.scenario: Match each feature of Harappan town planning to the effect it actually had.

slots.label: Cities built on a grid pattern with streets crossing at right angles
Every house connected to a covered underground drainage system
A large citadel built on a raised platform, separate from the lower town

components.label: Allowed the city to expand rapidly with no planning at all
Set apart important buildings for rulers or priests from ordinary homes
Kept waste water away from homes and helped maintain public health
Made it easier to organize traffic, buildings and public spaces in an orderly city

payload.hint: Think about what problem each planning choice actually solved for the people living there.

payload.scenario: Match each Harappan practice around trade to what it actually tells historians.

slots.label: Harappan traders used standardized weights and measures across the region
Seals carved with animals and an undeciphered script were used on goods
Harappan beads and cotton cloth have been found as far away as Mesopotamia

components.label: Proves Harappans and Mesopotamians spoke exactly the same language
Shows the Harappans were part of a wider long-distance trade network
Likely marked ownership or origin of goods, though the script still can't be read
Made trade fair and consistent, since buyers and sellers everywhere used the same units

payload.hint: Be careful with the seals — historians know they were used for something, but the script itself has never been deciphered.

title: Building and Running a Harappan City

scrambled_events.label: Merchants use the well-planned city's roads to set up trade with distant regions
City planners lay out streets in an organized grid pattern
Engineers build drains and wells to manage the city's water supply

payload.hint: The physical layout of the city had to exist before its water systems could be built into it, and both had to be in place before trade could flourish through it.

title: The Decline of the Harappan Civilisation

scrambled_events.label: Changes in climate and rivers make farming and trade harder to sustain
Cities are gradually abandoned as people move to find better conditions elsewhere
The Harappan civilisation reaches its peak, with extensive trade across long distances

payload.hint: A civilisation has to reach a peak before it can decline — think about what conditions had to worsen before people would leave their cities.

title: Speed Round: Angles on a Straight Line and Around a Point

payload.hint: Angles on a straight line add up to 180°; angles that go all the way around a point add up to 360°.

questions.prompt: Two angles on a straight line are 110° and x. Find x.
Three angles around a point are 90°, 120°, and x. Find x.
Two angles on a straight line are 65° and x. Find x.
Four angles around a point are 90°, 90°, 90°, and x. Find x.
Two angles on a straight line are 148° and x. Find x.
Three angles around a point are 100°, 140°, and x. Find x.

payload.hint: Vertically opposite angles (formed by two crossing lines) are always equal; angles next to each other on the same straight line are supplementary (add to 180°).

questions.prompt: Two lines cross, forming a 70° angle on one side. Find the angle vertically opposite to it.
Two lines cross, forming a 115° angle. Find its vertically opposite angle.
Two lines cross, forming angles of 40° and x next to each other on a straight line. Find x.
Two lines cross, forming a 25° angle. Find its vertically opposite angle.
Two lines cross, forming angles of 162° and x next to each other on a straight line. Find x.
Two lines cross, forming a 90° angle. Find its vertically opposite angle.

payload.scenario: Match each everyday material to what a magnet does to it, and why.

components.label: Not attracted — plastic has no magnetic material in it
Attracted — because it is shiny
Attracted — cobalt is one of the magnetic metals
Not attracted — aluminium is not one of the magnetic metals

payload.hint: Only iron, nickel, cobalt, and materials made from them are magnetic — aluminium and plastic are not.

payload.hint: A magnet attracts iron and steel objects, but has no effect on wood — and not every metal is magnetic.

payload.scenario: Magnet behaviour goes beyond just attraction. Match each situation to what actually happens.

slots.label: Bringing two North poles close together
Bringing a North pole and a South pole close together
Holding a magnet near a piece of gold

components.label: Nothing happens — gold isn't magnetic
The poles repel
The gold becomes permanently magnetized
The poles attract

payload.hint: Like poles push apart, unlike poles pull together — and gold isn't one of the magnetic metals.

payload.scenario: ஒவ்வொரு பழமொழிக்கும் சரியான பொருளைப் பொருத்துக.

எல்லாம் ஒரு நாள் நடக்கும் என்ற உறுதி
செய்த செயலுக்கேற்ப பலன் கிடைக்கும்

payload.hint: முதல் பழமொழி நேரம் ஆனாலும் நடக்கும் என்பதைப் பற்றியது; இரண்டாவது விதைத்ததற்கேற்ப அறுவடை என்பதைப் பற்றியது.

payload.scenario: மூன்று பழமொழிகளுக்கும் சரியான பொருளைப் பொருத்துக.

components.label: எல்லோரும் ஒரே நேரத்தில் தண்ணீர் குடிக்க வேண்டும்

payload.hint: ஒவ்வொரு பழமொழியும் வெவ்வேறு அறிவுரையை சொல்கிறது — பொறுமை, நல்வினை, செய்த செயலின் பலன்.

payload.scenario: ஒவ்வொரு பழமொழிக்கும் சரியான பொருளைப் பொருத்துக.

components.label: எப்போதும் அதிகமாகப் பேசுவதே சிறந்தது
சிறியது என்று எதையும் குறைவாக மதிப்பிடக் கூடாது
தேவைக்கு மேல் பேசாமல் இருப்பதே பெரும்பாலும் நல்லது

payload.hint: முதல் பழமொழி பேச்சில் அளவைப் பற்றியது; இரண்டாவது கடுகைப் போல சிறியதன் திறமையைப் பற்றியது.

payload.scenario: மூன்று பழமொழிகளுக்கும் சரியான பொருளைப் பொருத்துக.

components.label: எல்லோரும் ஒரே மாதிரி நடந்துகொள்ள வேண்டும்
நல்ல நட்பு நம் குணத்தையும் வழியையும் நல்லதாக்கும்
பயிற்சியும் முயற்சியும் சாதாரண திறனையும் சிறப்பானதாக மாற்றும்
தொடர்ந்து செய்யும் சிறு செயல்கள் காலப்போக்கில் பெரிய மாற்றத்தை உருவாக்கும்

payload.hint: ஒவ்வொன்றும் வெவ்வேறு அறிவுரை — தொடர் செயலின் பலன், பயிற்சியின் மேன்மை, நல்ல நட்பு.
